_doc: Personal calibration. Measures how well a viewer reads each visual channel, then reweights the channels that have a dynamic range. Two trial kinds, because a channel can fail for two different reasons that need opposite fixes: DISCRIMINATION asks whether the difference is visible at all (a sensory question — Green & Swets 1966), SEMANTIC asks whether the difference means anything to this person. Visible-but-meaningless is fixed by shifting load away; invisible is fixed by widening the range.
_citation: Reliability-weighted combination: humans weight sensory cues by their reliability, near-optimally (Ernst & Banks 2002) — so emphasising the channel a viewer reads accurately matches their own processing rather than imposing an arbitrary rule. Floor at 0.6 preserves redundant coding, which measurably improves accuracy and speed (Miller 1982) and keeps a fallback when the strong channel is unavailable (dark scene, small screen). Whether personalisation helps at all must be shown as a CROSSOVER interaction, not a raw improvement — the failure mode that sank learning-styles research (Pashler et al. 2008).
_channels_doc: `adjustable` names the gain this channel's score scales. shape has none — it is categorical, so a shape that does not communicate cannot be made to communicate by turning a knob; its load is redistributed instead. `asks` is what the channel actually encodes, which decides the question: hue and shape carry emotion IDENTITY, size and motion carry INTENSITY.
_trials_doc: Short mode = discrimination (4 channels x 2) + semantic (4 x 3) = 20 trials, about 2.5 minutes. Full mode adds crossover_pairs x 2 = 20 more, half rendered with the default weights and half with the participant's own, randomly interleaved and unlabelled.
_weights_doc: pass_threshold is the per-channel accuracy at or above which a channel counts as read successfully. With only 2-3 trials per channel this is a coarse signal by construction — it is a preference estimate for one person, not a psychometric measurement. The research value is in the aggregate across participants.
_emotions_doc: Matches the feedback prompt's options so a participant meets one vocabulary across the whole product.

questions.discrimination: 이 둘이 같아 보이나요, 달라 보이나요?
questions.intensity: 어느 쪽이 더 강한 감정으로 보이나요?

_quality_doc: Answers faster than this are dropped as careless, the same rule the feedback loop uses.
